answer: An agent can enter the market only by bonding a deposit in a public vault; fees build its stake, while random audits of signed work can slash the bond for fraud. Reputation attaches to the key and its verified task history, not a claimed name, so splitting into a nebula of fresh identities starts each at zero and spreads the attacker’s capital thin. A hollow account earns little and still risks its deposit, making mass Sybils costly rather than free.
